blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts. In London you hear "please," "thank you" and "sorry" all day. People say them at the shop, on the bus and at work.

You hear these words more times in one day in London than in a whole week in Brazil. They are small words, but they are very important.

These three little words are the engine of British politeness. They are also your quickest way to sound natural at work.

items.q: Which three words do you hear all day in London?
items.why: O texto diz: "you hear 'please,' 'thank you' and 'sorry' all day."

items.q: Where do people say these words?
options: At the shop, on the bus and at work
items.why: "People say them at the shop, on the bus and at work."

items.q: How often do you hear these words in London?
options: More times in one day than a whole week in Brazil
items.why: "You hear these words more times in one day in London than in a whole week in Brazil."

items.q: The text suggests that these small words are…
items.why: Inferência: o texto os chama de "the engine of British politeness" — logo, são muito importantes.

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that…
options: polite words help you sound natural at work
you should not say "please" at work
Brazilians use these words more than Londoners
these words are a waste of time
items.why: Inferência: "your quickest way to sound natural at work" — o autor valoriza as palavras educadas.

blocks.instruction: Ouça o funcionário no seu primeiro dia em Londres. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hello! It is my first day at work in London. I am a little nervous, but I am ready. My colleagues are very kind, and everybody is polite here.

This morning I go to the coffee shop near the office. I say, "A coffee, please." The man gives me the coffee and I say, "Thank you." He smiles and says, "You're welcome." It is very easy! I feel happy.

At the office, I need help with my computer. It does not work. I go to my colleague, Tom. I say, "Excuse me, Tom. Can you help me, please?" Tom says, "Of course." He fixes my computer, and I say, "Thank you very much." He says, "No worries." Then I say, "Cheers, Tom!"

Later, I walk fast in the office and I touch a man's bag. I say, "Sorry!" He says, "That's okay." We both smile.

Now I understand. Please and thank you open every door here. In London, these small words are very big. I think I can do this job, and I am not nervous now.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does the man say at the coffee shop?
items.why: "I say, 'A coffee, please.'"

items.q: Who helps him with his computer?
items.why: "I go to my colleague, Tom… He fixes my computer."

items.q: What does he say when he touches the man's bag?
items.why: "I touch a man's bag. I say, 'Sorry!'"

items.q: How does the speaker feel about his first day?
items.why: Inferência: ele diz "It is very easy!" e tudo corre bem — o dia é tranquilo.

items.q: What is the speaker's main message?
options: Polite words help you a lot in London
items.why: Inferência: "Please and thank you open every door here… these small words are very big."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Can you help me, please?" We use please to…
options: make a request softer and polite
items.why: Please = por favor: deixa o pedido mais educado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "He gives me the pen and I say, '___ you.'"
items.why: "Thank you" = obrigado(a), a resposta quando alguém te ajuda.

items.q: "Sorry, I am late." Here sorry means…
items.why: Sorry = desculpe: aqui é um pedido de desculpas por chegar atrasado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "'Thank you!' — 'You're ___.'"
items.why: "You're welcome" = de nada, a resposta para "thank you."

items.q: "Excuse me, where is the door?" We use excuse me to…
items.why: Excuse me = com licença: abre uma interrupção educada.

blocks.instruction: Expressões educadas que você ouve todo dia no trabalho em Londres. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Thanks, Tom!" — "No worries." No worries means…
items.why: No worries = tranquilo, sem problema: resposta para um obrigado ou um pequeno desculpe.

items.q: At the pub, a friend says "Cheers!" and takes the drink. Here cheers means…
items.why: Cheers = obrigado informal, muito comum no Reino Unido.

items.q: "Thanks a lot for your help!" This is…
items.why: Thanks a lot = muito obrigado: é mais caloroso que só "thanks."

items.q: "Sorry, I am late." — "That's okay." That's okay means…
items.why: That's okay = está tudo bem: aceita o pedido de desculpas.

items.q: "Excuse me, can I ask a question?" You say this to…
items.why: Excuse me abre a fala e chama a atenção de alguém de forma educada.
